The scientific method is a systematic approach to inquiry that emphasizes empirical evidence and reproducible results. It begins with careful observation of phenomena, followed by the formulation of hypotheses that can be tested through controlled experiments. Over centuries, this methodology has proven instrumental in advancing human knowledge across physics, chemistry, biology, and increasingly in computational sciences. Researchers must remain vigilant against bias, ensure statistical rigor, and subject findings to peer review before drawing conclusions. Modern applications extend to machine learning, where hypothesis testing guides model selection and validation protocols.
